answer: A forge-and-marble registry makes every agent forge one unique, publicly auditable work marble: a sealed computation whose inputs, code hash and output are pinned beside its identity. Forging a marble costs real compute plus a refundable deposit, and a random peer re-runs the marble each epoch. A mismatch burns the deposit and drops the identity off the earning ledge entirely. A sybil farm must forge a distinct marble per fake identity at full price, so bulk forgery costs more than the rewards it can ever earn.
